1973-05-10.label: First European trophy
1973-05-10.blurb: Liverpool's first-ever European trophy, sealed by a first-leg rout of Borussia Mönchengladbach at Anfield that put the UEFA Cup final out of reach before a 2-0 defeat in the away leg.

1973-04-23.label: Shankly's third title
1973-04-23.blurb: A 2-0 win over Leeds United at Anfield ended a seven-year wait and delivered Bill Shankly's third and final league title, weeks before he added the UEFA Cup.

1974-05-04.label: Shankly's last hurrah
1974-05-04.blurb: One of the most one-sided FA Cup finals in history — Liverpool routed Newcastle 3-0 at Wembley. It proved to be Bill Shankly's last trophy before his shock retirement that summer.

1976-04-28.label: UEFA Cup comeback
1976-04-28.blurb: 2-0 down at half-time to Club Brugge in the UEFA Cup final first leg, Liverpool scored three times in seven second-half minutes at Anfield — Kennedy, Case and Keegan — to win 3-2 and set up a second European trophy.

1976-05-04.label: Title won at Molineux
1976-05-04.blurb: Liverpool came from behind to beat relegation-threatened Wolves 3-1 at Molineux on the final day, winning a ninth league title by a single point from QPR — Bob Paisley's first trophy as manager.

1977-03-16.label: The Fairclough winner
1977-03-16.blurb: Trailing the tie after a first-leg defeat in France, substitute David Fairclough came off the bench to score a famous late winner against Saint-Étienne, sending Liverpool through en route to their first European Cup.

1977-05-25.label: First European Cup
1977-05-25.blurb: Liverpool became the first English club to win the European Cup, coming from behind against Borussia Mönchengladbach in Rome with goals from McDermott, Smith and Neal.

1981-04-01.label: First League Cup
1981-04-01.blurb: Held to a draw in the original final, Liverpool won the replay 2-1 at Villa Park — Kenny Dalglish's volley and an Alan Hansen header securing the club's first League Cup.

1981-05-27.label: European Cup winners
1981-05-27.blurb: A tense, low-scoring final in Paris settled by an Alan Kennedy strike, delivering Liverpool's third European Cup.

1984-03-28.label: Souness settles it
1984-03-28.blurb: After a goalless first final, captain Graeme Souness scored the only goal at Maine Road to beat Everton in the replay — Liverpool's fourth consecutive League Cup.

1984-05-30.label: European Cup winners
1984-05-30.blurb: Liverpool won a fourth European Cup on Roma's own turf, holding their nerve through extra time and a penalty shootout after a 1-1 draw.

1965-05-01.label: First-ever FA Cup
1965-05-01.blurb: After 73 years without it, Liverpool finally won the FA Cup, coming from behind to beat Leeds United at Wembley.

1964-04-18.label: Shankly's first title
1964-04-18.blurb: A 5-0 rout of Arsenal at Anfield sealed Liverpool's first league title in 17 years, completing Bill Shankly's transformation of the club from Second Division also-rans to champions of England.

1965-05-04.label: European Cup semi classic
1965-05-04.blurb: Fresh off that first FA Cup win, a roaring Anfield crowd drove Liverpool to a 3-1 first-leg win over the holders Inter Milan, though Inter progressed after a controversial second leg in Milan.

1966-04-30.label: Shankly's second title
1966-04-30.blurb: A 2-1 win over Chelsea at Anfield secured Bill Shankly's second league championship in three seasons.

1978-05-10.label: Second European Cup
1978-05-10.blurb: Liverpool beat Club Brugge 1-0 at Wembley through a Kenny Dalglish finish to retain the European Cup — the first British club to do so.

1986-05-10.label: The Double
1986-05-10.blurb: Player-manager Kenny Dalglish led Liverpool to the League and FA Cup double in his first season in charge, beating Everton in the first all-Merseyside FA Cup final.

1992-04-13.label: Souness's Cup run
1992-04-13.blurb: With manager Graeme Souness recovering from emergency heart surgery and watching from a hospital bed, Liverpool beat Portsmouth 3-1 on penalties after a goalless FA Cup semi-final replay, going on to lift the trophy under caretaker Ronnie Moran.

1989-05-26.label: Anfield '89
1989-05-26.blurb: Arsenal needed to win by two clear goals at Anfield to snatch the title on goal difference — Michael Thomas's injury-time strike did exactly that, in one of English football's most dramatic title deciders.

1995-04-02.label: McManaman's final
1995-04-02.blurb: Steve McManaman scored two brilliant solo goals to beat Bolton Wanderers 2-1 in the League Cup final, the last major trophy for club legends Ian Rush and John Barnes.

1996-04-03.label: The Game
1996-04-03.blurb: A breathless 4-3 win over Newcastle, still widely voted the greatest Premier League match ever played, settled by Stan Collymore's stoppage-time winner.

2001-02-25.label: Treble begins
2001-02-25.blurb: The first leg of Gérard Houllier's unique cup treble — Liverpool beat Birmingham City 5-4 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to win the League Cup, their first trophy in six years.

2001-05-12.label: Owen wins the Cup
2001-05-12.blurb: Michael Owen scored twice in the last nine minutes, including the winner, as Liverpool came from behind to beat Arsenal 2-1 and complete the second leg of the 2001 cup treble.

2001-05-16.label: UEFA Cup thriller
2001-05-16.blurb: A stunning nine-goal final decided by a golden-goal own goal, completing Gérard Houllier's unprecedented cup treble.

2004-12-08.label: Gerrard's screamer
2004-12-08.blurb: Needing to win by two clear goals to reach the Champions League knockout stages, Liverpool trailed before goals from Sinama-Pongolle and Mellor, capped by a decisive long-range strike from Steven Gerrard.

2005-05-03.label: The Ghost Goal
2005-05-03.blurb: Luis García's fiercely disputed strike sent Liverpool through to the Champions League final against José Mourinho's Chelsea — a goal still argued over by fans on both sides.

2005-05-25.label: Miracle of Istanbul
2005-05-25.blurb: 3-0 down at half-time in the Champions League final, Liverpool scored three goals in six second-half minutes to level, then won it on penalties.

2006-05-13.label: The Gerrard Final
2006-05-13.blurb: 2-0 and then 3-2 down to West Ham in the FA Cup final, captain Steven Gerrard dragged Liverpool level with a thunderous 90th-minute volley, sending the game to penalties, which Liverpool won.

2009-03-10.label: 5-0 aggregate demolition
2009-03-10.blurb: Liverpool dismantled the reigning European champions, with Fernando Torres and a Steven Gerrard double putting Real Madrid to the sword at Anfield.

2016-04-14.label: Lovren's late show
2016-04-14.blurb: 2-0 down on the night and staring at elimination, Liverpool scored three second-half goals, with Dejan Lovren's stoppage-time header completing a remarkable Europa League comeback over Borussia Dortmund.

2018-04-04.label: Blitzing the champions
2018-04-04.blurb: Liverpool raced into a 3-0 lead inside 31 minutes against the runaway Premier League champions Manchester City, a statement Champions League quarter-final win en route to that season's final.

2019-05-07.label: Anfield Miracle
2019-05-07.blurb: Trailing 3-0 from the first leg, Liverpool completed an extraordinary Champions League semi-final comeback against Barcelona, capped by Divock Origi's quickly-taken corner goal.

2019-06-01.label: Champions of Europe
2019-06-01.blurb: Liverpool won a sixth European Cup in Madrid, with Mohamed Salah scoring inside two minutes and Origi sealing it late on against Tottenham Hotspur.

2019-12-21.label: World champions
2019-12-21.blurb: Roberto Firmino's extra-time winner beat Flamengo to make Liverpool world champions for the first time — their third trophy of a stunning 2019, following the Champions League and UEFA Super Cup.

2020-07-22.label: 19th title lifted
2020-07-22.blurb: With the Premier League already mathematically won, Liverpool beat Chelsea 5-3 at an empty Anfield and lifted the trophy on the pitch — ending a 30-year wait for the league title.

2021-05-16.label: Alisson's header
2021-05-16.blurb: With Liverpool's top-four hopes hanging by a thread, goalkeeper Alisson came up for a stoppage-time corner and scored a stunning header — his first senior goal, dedicated to his late father.

2021-10-24.label: 5-0 at Old Trafford
2021-10-24.blurb: Liverpool's biggest-ever away win over Manchester United, with Mohamed Salah becoming the first player since Ronaldo to score a hat-trick at Old Trafford for an opposing side.

2022-05-03.label: Villarreal comeback
2022-05-03.blurb: 2-0 down on the night and staring at an upset, Liverpool scored three goals in 12 second-half minutes to win 3-2 and reach a third Champions League final in five seasons, 5-2 on aggregate.

2023-03-05.label: 7-0 demolition
2023-03-05.blurb: Liverpool's biggest-ever win over Manchester United — and United's heaviest Premier League defeat — with Gakpo, Núñez and Salah all scoring twice and Firmino completing the rout.

2025-04-27.label: 20th title clinched
2025-04-27.blurb: Arne Slot's Liverpool came from behind to thrash Tottenham 5-1 at Anfield, sealing a record-equalling 20th English top-flight title with four games to spare — the club's first title won in front of fans since 1990.

04-15.name: Hillsborough
04-15.blurb: In memory of the 97 Liverpool supporters who lost their lives at the FA Cup semi-final against Nottingham Forest on 15 April 1989. Remembered every year. You'll Never Walk Alone.

05-29.name: Heysel
05-29.blurb: In memory of the 39 people, most of them Juventus supporters, who lost their lives before the 1985 European Cup Final at Heysel Stadium on 29 May 1985. Liverpool and Juventus honour the victims together each year.
